construct: Titin is a giant sarcomeric protein spanning from the Z-disc toward the M-line. Elastic elements in its I-band region behave as molecular springs during stretch, generating passive tension and restoring sarcomere length. Titin is therefore a major determinant of passive stiffness and elasticity in skeletal and cardiac muscle.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Stretching a relaxed sarcomere without cross-bridge cycling isolates passive elastic force; the extensible I-band regions of titin act as the principal sarcomeric molecular spring.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Nebulin is a sarcomeric structural protein and therefore the strongest distractor, but it primarily organizes thin-filament architecture rather than generating longitudinal passive restoring force.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only titin directly supplies the spring-like passive tension described while actin and myosin remain intact.
